edges.description: Sustained mitogenic RAS-MAPK signaling drives clonal proliferation and neoplastic transformation of thyroid follicular cells into papillary thyroid carcinoma.
Persistent oncogenic MAPK output suppresses thyroid follicular differentiation transcriptional programs.
PI3K-AKT survival and proliferative signaling promotes clonal expansion of transformed papillary thyroid carcinoma cells.
Chronic PI3K-AKT pathway activation contributes to loss of differentiated thyroid follicular identity in progressive disease.
Loss of thyroid follicular differentiation directly downregulates sodium/iodide symporter (NIS/SLC5A5) expression and impairs cellular radioiodine uptake.

edges.description: Loss of radioiodine avidity allows persistent and metastatic tumor lesions to escape radioiodine ablation and progress clinically.

edges.description: Clonal papillary tumor growth within the thyroid gland presents clinically or ultrasonographically as a thyroid nodule.
Malignant follicular-cell transformation produces histopathologically confirmed papillary thyroid carcinoma.
Primary RET fusion-positive papillary thyroid carcinomas—even at the microcarcinoma stage—frequently invade lymphatic and vascular channels to seed regional lymph node and distant metastases.
Lymphatic dissemination of papillary thyroid carcinoma cells to regional neck compartments produces metastatic cervical lymphadenopathy.
Hematogenous dissemination of RET fusion-positive thyroid carcinoma cells establishes distant organ metastases in 18.6% of patients.

Ionizing radiation induces DNA double-strand breaks in thyroid follicular cells that promote intrachromosomal inversions and translocations generating oncogenic RET fusions, particularly NCOA4::RET in young children.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic treatments for radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancers
evidence.snippet: Recent research has revealed that the genetic mutations and gene rearrangements affecting sites such as RTKs, RAS, BRAF and TERTp lead to structural and functional abnormalities in encoded proteins. These abnormalities aberrantly activate signaling pathways like the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and phosphatidylinositol-3-hydroxykinase (PI3K) signaling pathways, resulting in thyroid cells dedifferentiation, sodium/iodide symporter (NIS) dysfunction, and consequent the RAI-refractory nature of DTCs.

nodes.description: Selective small-molecule RET tyrosine kinase inhibitor approved for advanced or metastatic radioiodine-refractory RET fusion-positive thyroid carcinoma, achieving a 90.9% objective response rate among previously treated RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer patients in the ARROW trial (NCT03037385).

evidence.reference_title: Systemic treatments for radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancers
evidence.snippet: Pralsetinib is another strong RET inhibitor. In the ARROW study (NCT03037385), the ORR of pralsetinib in 22 previously treated RET fusion positive thyroid cancer patients was 90.9% (95%CI: 70.8-98.9) (149).

evidence.reference_title: RET-Altered Cancers—A Tumor-Agnostic Review of Biology, Diagnosis and Targeted Therapy Activity
evidence.snippet: Targeted therapies for RET-dependent cancers have evolved from older multikinase inhibitors to selective inhibitors of RET such as selpercatinib and pralsetinib. Prospective basket trials and retrospective reports have demonstrated the activity of these drugs in a wide variety of RET-altered cancers, notably those with RET fusions.

nodes.description: Adjuvant radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy is administered selectively after surgery for intermediate- or high-risk RET fusion-positive differentiated thyroid cancer that retains sodium/iodide symporter-mediated iodine avidity.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic treatments for radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancers
evidence.snippet: Due to DTCs’ distinctive radioiodine (RAI) uptake mechanism, standard treatment involving surgery, with or without adjunctive therapy using RAI and levothyroxine inhibition, typically yields favorable prognoses for the majority of patients with DTCs.

nodes.description: Highly selective ATP-competitive small-molecule RET kinase inhibitor approved for advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer requiring systemic therapy and radioiodine-refractory if RAI is appropriate, achieving high and durable objective response rates in LIBRETTO-001.

evidence.reference_title: Durability of Response With Selpercatinib in Patients With RET-Activated Thyroid Cancer: Long-Term Safety and Efficacy From LIBRETTO-001
evidence.snippet: We present long-term safety and efficacy from LIBRETTO-001 in patients with RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC; n = 324) and RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer encompassing different histological subtypes (TC; n = 66). At the data cutoff of January 2023, the objective response rate was 82.5% among patients with cabozantinib/vandetanib-naïve MTC and 95.8% among patients with treatment-naïve TC.

evidence.reference_title: FDA Approval Summary: Selpercatinib for the Treatment of Advanced RET Fusion-Positive Solid Tumors
evidence.snippet: The recommendation for approval was supported by results from LIBRETTO-001 in patients with RET fusion-positive NSCLC and thyroid cancer, which formed the basis of prior approvals in these tumor types.
